programme: ID4 and TRIM28 form a cell-cycle-restraint/differentiation-checkpoint circuit: ID4, a dominant-negative HLH regulator, gates against illegitimate proliferation by sitting upstream of TP53, BRCA1, CREBBP, SOX2 and IGF1R, while TRIM28 (KAP1) co-represses the E2F-family cell-cycle effectors E2F3/E2F4 and the ID4 paralog ID1 — the same corepressor axis that keeps a terminally-specified cell (post-mitotic neuron or luminal epithelial cell) out of the cycle.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, ID4 is implicated directly in restraining aberrant cell-cycle re-entry in post-mitotic neurons (PMID 32708313), a long-recognised route to neuronal death; TRIM28 separately regulates aggresome/proteostasis handling (PMID 33783327), the kind of downstream proteotoxic stress response expected when this checkpoint fails.
role_in_b: In prostate cancer, ID4 is required for luminal epithelial terminal differentiation and its restoration/delivery suppresses tumour growth (PMID 33884281, 27487149); TRIM28 forms a documented feedback loop with E2F1 that drives castration-resistant progression (PMID 40519166, matching its E2F3/E2F4 targets here), alongside roles in CRPC metabolic reprogramming (PMID 41105391) and immune-checkpoint correlation (PMID 38958986).
shared_axis: Post-mitotic neurons and terminally-differentiated luminal prostate epithelium both depend on an Id/E2F-TRIM28 checkpoint to stay out of the cell cycle; when ID4's restraint or TRIM28's E2F repression fails, neurons re-enter the cycle and degenerate (AD) while luminal cells lose differentiation and gain proliferative, castration-resistant capacity (PC) — the same checkpoint machinery guarding a different differentiated state in each tissue.
reasoning: Each factor is independently placed by retrieved papers in both diseases, and cell-cycle-checkpoint dysregulation is separately well established in AD neurodegeneration and in E2F/Rb-pathway-driven prostate cancer, so the axis is real in each disease on its own; but no retrieved paper connects the two diseases through it, the AD TRIM28 paper concerns proteostasis rather than cell-cycle re-entry directly, and the counts (ID4 80/136, TRIM28 73/136) are moderate rather than near-unanimous.
support: PMID 32708313 - ID4 implicated in neuronal cell-cycle re-entry in AD; PMID 33884281 - ID4 required for luminal epithelial terminal differentiation in prostate; PMID 27487149 - ID4 protein delivery inhibits prostate tumour growth; PMID 33783327 - TRIM28 negatively regulates aggresome formation, an AD-relevant proteostasis role; PMID 40519166 - RSK1-driven TRIM28/E2F1 feedback loop drives castration-resistant prostate cancer progression, matching TRIM28's E2F3/E2F4 targets in this network; PMID 41105391 - TRIM28-LDHA axis regulates bone metastatic prostate cancer; PMID 38958986 - TRIM28 expression correlates with immune checkpoints in CRPC.
how_to_falsify: In parallel, knock down ID4 and TRIM28 in (1) a human iPSC-derived post-mitotic neuron model and (2) an androgen-deprived CRPC cell line, and profile E2F-target/cell-cycle genes (e.g. CCNB1, PCNA, cyclin D1, phospho-Rb); the checkpoint model predicts coordinated de-repression of the same E2F-target signature and, in neurons, markers of cell-cycle re-entry preceding death. If loss of these factors produces non-overlapping transcriptional consequences in the two systems, or if E2F targets are unaffected in either model, the shared-checkpoint account fails.
caveats: Brain and prostate are anatomically and clinically unrelated, so any shared axis here is a cell-biology parallel, not a documented cross-disease fact; supported by 136 patient-group comparisons across only 6 independent cohort pairs, and neither carrying factor is near-unanimous (ID4 80/136, TRIM28 73/136). Higher-recurrence factors such as SP100 (112/136) and ERG (101/136) were deliberately excluded from the module: SP100 has no paper placing it in either disease, and ERG's retrieved 'AD' hits are confounded by unrelated uses of the term (exponential random graphs, electroretinography) despite strong prostate-cancer and Open Targets support. The tissue-generic exclusion list (SOX10, ZEB1, NOTCH1, TAL1, etc.) confirms this account does not lean on a generic neural/epithelial master regulator, and the single-view exclusions (SF1, PLAGL2, POU2F1, etc.) are correctly left out as one-cohort artifacts.
